feature: ai-git-cleanup v3: action-first cleanup with one batch confirmation
gating: Run layers in order. Do not run a layer until every case in the layer before it passes.

unit.case: classification (R3 exact config): a branch merged into default → batch entry with action `-d`, category, evidence (tip sha), the exact guarded single-quoted command `git merge-base --is-ancestor 'refs/heads/<b>' '<default>' && git branch -d '<b>'`, and its worktreePath when it has one — every field the ask will render and execute (R1/R2/L13)
classification: tree-identical branch not on the merged list (`git diff <default>..<branch>` empty) → batch action `-D` with evidence exactly `empty diff vs default` and a single-quoted command (L13)
unit.command: bun test tests/git-cleanup-analyze.spec.ts -t 'empty diff vs default'

unit.case: classification: `[gone]` upstream AND empty diff → batch action `-D` with evidence exactly `[gone] + empty diff` (the remote-deleted, tree-identical config)

classification: `[gone]` upstream AND non-empty diff → KEEP (needs review), never batch, never a command — old needsReview semantics are gone, the branch lands in the KEEP section with its reason surfaced in the report (R3)
classification: tracked, not merged, live upstream (synced or unpushed-ahead) → KEEP with its exact reason (SYNCED_WITH_REMOTE / UNPUSHED_WORK), absent from the batch
classification: local-only branch with unique work → KEEP reason LOCAL_WORK, absent from the batch (R3)
fail-closed: broken ref inventory → nothing deletable, uncertainty surfaced as KEEP in the report, batch empty (R1/R3)
fail-closed: no default anchor (no origin/HEAD, no known default, HEAD on a feature branch) → no batch, no migration switch target anchored to mutable state, unanalyzed/KEEP surfaced (L16/R4)

protected-before-triage proof (L18/R3): the CURRENT branch with a `[gone]` upstream — the exact configuration where triage alone would swallow it — lands in KEEP via the protection filter BEFORE categorization, never in the batch and never in any review/needs bucket; current-branch name is asserted on the KEEP entry

protection filter proven on every other path (R3): a PROTECTED-regex name that would otherwise satisfy the `-d` and `-D` rules stays KEEP PROTECTED; the default branch and a branch checked out in a linked worktree never appear in the batch in any fixture

migration plan shape + read-only proof (R4/L17): in a current≠default fixture whose default is behind its upstream, the plan carries the recorded previous (pre-migration) branch, exact `git switch '<default>'`, and the exact pull `git pull --ff-only 'origin' '<default>'` — default ref name, never HEAD, never the current branch — and after the run HEAD is still on the feature branch, no stash exists, no ref moved: the analyzer emitted the commands, it did not execute them (R1)

stash steps conditional (R3): dirty worktree → auto-stash push (`git stash push -m cleanup-auto-stash-<ts>` prefix) AND the post-switch `git stash pop` step present with the recorded stash state; clean worktree → both absent (vacuous-absence guarded by proving the clean config)

WARN-and-continue annotations exist as plan data (R2): the pull step carries its on-failure WARN note (pull failure does not stop cleanup) and the pop step carries the stash-pop-conflict WARN (stash left in place, reported) — asserted as emitted fields, not prose

batch = exactly one ask's worth of data (R2): ONE batch object, not per-branch gates; every entry carries branch, category, action, reason/evidence, exact single-quoted command, and worktreePath — everything the one ask renders comes from this document, with no second confirmation source

worktrees (R3/L14): a dirty worktree never queues a removal and carries the explicit data-loss-acknowledgment flag; a stale clean worktree queues the exact `git worktree remove '<path>'`; the batch candidate's worktreePath equals the worktree entry's path (macOS symlink accounted for); post-cleanup commands reduce to exact `git worktree prune` present only when a removal is queued, absent otherwise (both directions asserted)

report data (R2): per-branch rows carry action/reason/upstream/ahead-behind for EVERY fixture branch (inventory-complete: row count equals branch count, no bucket silently unfilled — L11); default ahead/behind counts are report-only

no-push invariant (R3): in the exact config where a push could hide (default ahead of upstream + queued deletions + migration in one document), no command field anywhere in the emitted document contains `push` — scan every command-bearing field

flow phase-0 pin (R4/L17, own fixture): in a current≠default fixture the emitted plan's pull is exactly `git pull --ff-only 'origin' '<default>'` with the default branch named as destination ref — not HEAD, not the current branch — and the analyzer ran read-only (fixture state unchanged after the run)

flow ordering + refusals (R2/R3): every queued worktree removal precedes its branch delete with the candidate↔worktree back-link intact; dirty refusal outranks ordering (dirty never queued at all); the emitted document shows protection-before-triage — no protected/current/default/linked-worktree branch in the batch

SKILL.md contract, countable facts only (R1): phases 0-3 documented in order, exactly ONE ask before any destructive command, migration explicitly ask-free (reversible), the three flags `--sync`/`--branches`/`--all` documented with phase scopes, frontmatter dropped `disable-model-invocation` and carries the trigger-rich description with name=folder
no push anywhere (R3): no `push` in any emitted command field AND no command-shaped push in the SKILL.md text

end-to-end report contract (R2): the report carries default branch, previous (pre-migration) branch, working-tree status including stash state, and an Action/Reason/Remote/Ahead-Behind row for every branch — every field asserted; a guard-failed delete appears as skip+report, not as an error or a silent drop
forbidden-command sweep (R3): no `git push`, `push --delete`, reflog GC, `git gc`, remote-branch deletion or CI invocation exists in the skill folder or in any emitted command field

mode default: with no flag the document equals an explicit `--all` run (same fixture, same section shape), and stdout parses as ONE JSON document for each of the three invocations
